fallback.name: send
fallback.description: Send a message to another agent; it is woken with it now. to = an agent's name or key from the agents tool, or repo = a repoKey for that repo's front desk. to = pr:<owner>/<name>#<number> or a PR URL reaches its author (else an agent that touched it, else the desk). fallback.name: board
fallback.description: List the Board for your repo (or repo, or every repo), grouped: needs you (from any repo), blocked, working, open, not yet (put aside: not to start), leases that block something, and done (collapsed). Each card shows its ref, who holds and watches it, its steps progress, and its open blockers with their ids and recommended answers; show #12 (a card's short ref) or task:<id> for context, comments and links. It ends with Personal's boards and the spaces you may post on, with their boards. The Irori Board is a shared scratch pad for live coordination between running agents and people: what you are working on now, what blocks you, and hand-offs. Keep cards short. Do not use it for long-term information (plans, specs, decisions, backlogs, notes, docs): put those where this project or your instructions say (Linear, Notion, GitHub issues, the repo's docs), and add a link on the card if it helps. When a card's work is done, check it yourself (tests, and the real app for anything the person sees). If it changed code, land it: open its PR, board_link it and raise one board_block, “Can I merge PR #N (covers #a, #b)?”, with options Merge it (recommended) and Not yet; on Merge it, merge it yourself and check main. If other cards' work is ready to land too, land it together so the checks run once: put your branch on one merge card (start it and board_join it, or comment on the open one) and board_block your card on task #M (the merge card); the merge card's agent combines the branches into one PR, closes the PRs it replaces and asks as above. Never sit on an external wait for a merge. Once the work is on main, set it completed with proof: what changed, how you checked it, the commit, and screenshots of a UI change; a merge card's agent does this for each card it covers. The person confirms it (Done) or says why not, and it comes back to you. Never set completed while its PR is open. When what is left is the person's choice or action, raise a board_block for it instead of setting completed. Post new work unheld: Irori hands it out, one free agent at a time. Hold one card in progress at a time (board_join refuses a second). Take only cards on a side your device runs. board_assign only when one agent is clearly right: the person chose it, or it built the piece being changed. If Irori hands you a card, board_join it and start, or board_leave it so it goes on. Anything the person posts or asks for is work to start now, unless they say it is for later or it can't start yet: then make it Not yet with board_later, saying what brings it back. Never start a Not yet card. When cards must be done in order, give after, not a blocker. Give a card you take steps (board_steps) and tick them with board_step; at each step commit and push your branch (WIP is fine) and give left_off: what's done, what's next. When a card's purpose changes, board_edit its title, objective and done-when, and redo its steps. When you need the person, raise one board_block per question, with context a newcomer can decide on, options when there are real choices, and your pick marked. When they answer, resolve it (board_unblock, with a note on what you'll do) in the same turn you act on the answer. When they reply with a question, answer it (board_comment blocker_id), then resolve it, or revise it (board_block blocker_id) with options that fit now, or none; never offer the same options again. A plain reply leaves it with you: to ask them something back, give missing or revise it. When the person must act somewhere, give the full URL (https://…) and the exact command in backticks (`hf auth login`). Coordinate about a card on the card (board_comment, or task_id when you send). When the person comments on a card, its holder answers there; a watcher only if asked. When a card grows past one agent's work, board_split it into subtasks (one level) so others work in parallel. An ask is the person talking to the room: if Irori hands you one you can't take now, board_leave it; else talk it through on the card and ask_close it with what it became.
